info.title: FreeDict API
info.summary: English dictionary data over HTTP: definitions, examples, pronunciation, synonyms, rhymes, word origins, slang, translations and word search.
info.description:
English dictionary data for apps, sites, games and AI agents: definitions, examples, pronunciation, synonyms, rhymes, word origins, slang, translations and one word search that takes every filter in a single call.

## Authentication

Send your key in the `X-API-Key` header on every request. Get a free key from https://freedict.com/account/api (a verified FreeDict account is needed). Keep it on your server.

## Responses

Every response is JSON. Successful responses wrap the result in `data` (with `meta`); errors come back as `error` with a `code` and a `message`, never with a 200 status.

## Plans and limits

Each plan has a monthly allowance and a per-minute limit. Batch, search and seeded-list requests have their own, smaller per-minute limit (a tenth of the plan's rate, never under 5). Only successful calls count towards the allowance. On paid plans, calls beyond the allowance keep working and are billed at the plan's overage rate; on the Free plan they stop until the 1st of the next month. A 429 carries `Retry-After`. Prices are on https://freedict.com/api/pricing.

| Plan | Calls a month | Requests a minute | Search, batch and seeded lists a minute |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 3,000 | 60 | 6 |
| Starter | 100,000 | 300 | 30 |
| Pro | 1,000,000 | 1,200 | 120 |
| Business | 5,000,000 | 3,000 | 300 |

On the Free plan, show a visible "Powered by FreeDict" link to https://freedict.com wherever you display the data; responses carry the text and link in `meta.attribution`. Cache and reuse rules are in the API terms: https://freedict.com/api/terms.

## AI apps

The same tools are available to AI apps through the MCP server at https://freedict.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE). See https://freedict.com/api/docs#mcp.

data.title: Affect vs effect — What's the difference?
data.quick_answer: "Affect" is almost always a verb meaning to influence or change something ("The rain affected our plans"). "Effect" is almost always a noun meaning a result ("The rain had no effect on our plans"). A quick trick: A is for Action (affect = verb), E is for End result (effect = noun).
data.explanation: These two words trip up even confident writers because they sound almost identical and both relate to cause and consequence — but they play different grammatical roles almost all of the time. The basic rule Affect is a verb. It means to influence, change, or have an impact on something. "Lack of sleep affects your concentration." Effect is a noun. It means a result or outcome. "Lack of sleep has a serious effect on your concentration." A trick to remember it Think: Affect = Action (a verb, something being done), Effect = End result (a noun, the thing that happened). If you can put "the" or "an" in front of the word, you almost certainly want "effect" — "the effect", "a side effect". The exceptions (why this trips people up) Both words have rarer opposite uses that catch people out: Effect can be a verb meaning "to bring about" or "to cause to happen" — usually in formal writing. "The new manager effected several changes to the schedule." Here it means she caused the changes to happen, not that she was influenced by them. Affect can be a noun in psychology, meaning a person's outward display of emotion. "The patient showed a flat affect." This is specialist usage — you're unlikely to need it outside clinical writing. For everyday writing, the simple rule (affect = verb, effect = noun) is right about 95% of the time. More examples "The medication may affect your appetite." (verb — influences) "The medication's effects include drowsiness." (noun — the results) "How will this policy affect small businesses?" (verb) "What effect will this policy have on small businesses?" (noun)

faqs.q: Is it "affect my life" or "effect my life"?
faqs.a: "Affect my life" — you want the verb, since something is influencing your life. "Effect" would only fit if you meant a noun, e.g. "the effect on my life."
Yes, though rarely — "to effect" means to bring something about or cause it to happen, as in "effect change." It's formal and much less common than "effect" the noun.

faqs.q: What's an easy way to remember affect vs effect?
faqs.a: Affect = Action (verb). Effect = End result (noun). If you can put "the" or "an" before it, it's almost always "effect."

get.description: One search for any mix of spelling (pattern t??k or un*able, starts, ends, contains, length), sound (sounds like, rhymes with), meaning ("ringing in the ears"), company (adjectives for a noun, what follows a word), kind-of and part-of, syllables, part of speech and CEFR level. get.summary: Word search or seeded word list
get.description: Without `seed` this is the same search as `GET /api/v1/words`. With `seed` it returns the words that match your filters in a fixed order for that seed, which is what word games need: the same seed always gives the same list, so a daily puzzle never changes after the day it was set. A seeded list needs the Pro plan or above; the sound, syllable and `include` filters cannot be mixed with a seed (422). A filter the API does not support is a 422, never ignored.

locked.description: Present when `include` named something your plan does not cover: the call still succeeds and lists what was left out.

PlanRequired.description: Your plan does not include this endpoint. The message names the plan that does.

error.message: The batch endpoint needs the Starter plan or above. See https://freedict.com/api/pricing

NotFound.description: The word is not in the dictionary (`word_not_found`; other lookups answer `not_found`). Close spellings may come back in `suggestions`. A missing word is never charged.

Invalid.description: Something in the request needs fixing; the message says what. Codes include `locale_required`, `unknown_locale`, `unknown_parameter`, `bad_pattern`, `bad_request`, `bad_include`, `bad_date`, `too_many`, `unknown_flag` and `filter_unavailable`. A parameter the API does not know is refused, never ignored.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests this minute (`rate_limited`, wait for `Retry-After`) or the Free plan month is used up (`quota_exceeded`).

QuotaLimit.description: Your monthly allowance. Sent on plans that have one.

QuotaUsed.description: How much of the monthly allowance you have used. Only successful calls count.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.
